title: توسعه مرحله‌ای Dino Dash از MVP تا نسخه نهایی
problem: محصول به فازهای روشن و قابل‌تحویل تقسیم شود: ابتدا MVP تک‌نفره با دویدن، پرش، موانع و امتیاز؛ سپس پروفایل و ذخیره پیشرفت؛ بعد کاراکترها و اقتصاد امتیازی؛ سپس جدول رتبه‌بندی و رقابت زنده با دوستان؛ و در پایان پرداخت بصری، پایداری، دسترس‌پذیری و آمادگی انتشار نسخه نهایی.
desiredOutcome: CANONICAL NON-GOALS TEXT, for any downstream author to cite verbatim rather than re-derive - this is the artifact ISS-20260809-011 asked for. 'For this version of Dino Dash, the following are NON-GOALS and are removed from scope, not deferred: real-time synchronous play; server-authoritative live session state; matchmaking, lobbies or race invitations; presence or online indicators; tick rate or update cadence; netcode interpolation, prediction or rollback; mid-run reconnection; and any latency, jitter or update-cadence budget. Live competition means compare-after-the-fact, per APR-870DC901FD68. For Unit 1 specifically the following are additionally non-goals: persistence of any kind, any network call, any identity, any leaderboard or score table, and any character beyond the single default.' Reopening any of these is a new product direction requiring the human product_direction_or_priority gate, not a delivery detail.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-01 | The game opens and becomes playable in a current desktop browser from a single entry point under src/, reaching an idle state with no sign-in, no loading dependency on any server, and no error in the browser console.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Open the entry point in a current Chromium-based browser and a current Gecko-based browser at 100% zoom. Record browser name and version. Observe the idle state renders. Confirm the console shows zero errors and the network panel shows zero cross-origin requests. Repeat in both browsers; both must pass.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-02 | The idle state displays a visible on-screen instruction telling the player how to start, and the run starts from the idle state using the keyboard alone, with no pointer input at any point.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: With the mouse and trackpad physically unused, read the instruction on screen, then press the key it names. A run begins. Reload and repeat using the alternative jump key. Both must start the run. Photograph or screenshot the idle state showing the instruction text.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-03 | During a run, each discrete press of the Space key while the character is grounded initiates exactly one jump: the character leaves the ground and returns to it.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Start a run using the keyboard. Press Space once. Observe one jump arc, one landing. Repeat ten times across one run; count jumps initiated and confirm the count equals the number of Space presses made while grounded. Holding Space must not produce continuous or repeated jumps.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-04 | During a run, each discrete press of the Up Arrow key while the character is grounded initiates exactly one jump, behaving identically to Space. Both keys are active for the entire session; neither is a mode, a setting, or a replacement for the other.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Repeat AC-03 using Up Arrow. Then within a single run alternate Space, Up Arrow, Space, Up Arrow and confirm all four jump. No configuration step, key rebinding or toggle may be required to make either key work.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-05 | Pressing Space or Up Arrow while the game is focused does not trigger the browser default action: the page does not scroll and no other document-level behaviour occurs.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Load the entry point in a viewport short enough that the page would scroll if the default fired. During a run press Space ten times and Up Arrow ten times. Confirm the document scroll position is unchanged throughout, measured before and after.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-06 | Contact between the character and a cactus ends the run: the run-end state is entered, the character stops, and the session score stops increasing.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Play until the character contacts a cactus. Observe the transition to the run-end state. Record the score displayed at the instant of contact and again five seconds later; the two values must be identical. Repeat three times.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-07 | Successfully clearing a cactus does not end the run. Only contact with a cactus ends it; no other event in Unit 1 does.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Play a run in which at least five cacti are cleared without contact and confirm the run continues after each. Confirm no timer, score threshold, key press or idle period ends the run. The only observed run-ending event across at least three runs must be cactus contact.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-08 | The session score is visible on screen continuously throughout a run. It starts at zero at the first frame of the run and never decreases.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Start a run and screenshot immediately: the displayed score reads zero. Screenshot at approximately two-second intervals until the run ends. Read the value from each screenshot in order and confirm the sequence is non-decreasing and that the score element is present in every frame.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-09 | The run-end state displays the final session score of the run that just ended, and that value equals the last value displayed during the run.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: End a run and compare the value on the run-end state against the last score value visible before contact, read from a screenshot taken within the final second of the run. The two must be identical. Repeat three times, including one run ended within five seconds of starting.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-10 | From the run-end state, the player can start a new run without refreshing or reloading the page. The new run's score starts at zero.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: End a run with a non-zero score. Trigger restart. Confirm a new run begins and the displayed score reads zero. Confirm no page load occurred: performance.getEntriesByType('navigation') still returns exactly one entry, and the network panel shows no new document request. Repeat five consecutive times without reloading.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-11 | The run-end state displays a visible on-screen instruction telling the player how to restart, and restart is operable by keyboard alone.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Screenshot the run-end state and confirm the restart instruction is legible. With the pointer unused, press the key the instruction names and confirm a new run begins.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-12 | The complete Unit 1 journey - open, start, jump, collide, restart, collide again - is completable using the keyboard alone. No function in Unit 1 requires a mouse, trackpad, touch or any pointing device.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Physically disconnect or refrain from using all pointing devices. Complete the full journey twice end to end. Record any step that could not be performed; the expected count of such steps is zero.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-13 | Restarting resets the run state completely: score to zero, character to its starting position, obstacles cleared. No value from the previous run persists into the new one.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Play a run to a score above zero, restart, and within the first second confirm the score reads zero, the character is at its start position, and no obstacle from the previous run is on screen. Repeat after a long run and after a run ended immediately.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-14 | Wherever a focusable control exists in any of the three states, keyboard focus is visibly indicated, focus order is predictable, and focus is never trapped in a state the keyboard cannot leave.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: In each of idle, running and run-end, press Tab repeatedly through a full cycle and screenshot every focus stop. Confirm each stop shows a visible focus indicator and that continuing to press Tab returns to the first stop. Confirm Tab never becomes unresponsive.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-15 | No keyboard interaction in Unit 1 depends on a key the player is not told about. Every key that has an effect - start, jump, restart - is named in on-screen instruction text at the state where it applies.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: List every key with an observable effect by testing Space, Up Arrow, Enter, Escape, Tab and arrow keys in each state. Compare that list against the keys named in on-screen text. Any key with an effect that is not named on screen fails this criterion.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-16 | Every piece of text presented to the player - the score readout, the start instruction, the run-end text and the restart instruction - has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against the background actually rendered behind it, in every state and against every background variation the text appears over. This is the owner's WCAG AA threshold.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Capture screenshots of each text element in each state, including at least two different background conditions during a run. Sample the rendered foreground and background pixel values and compute the WCAG contrast ratio for each. Record the measured ratio per element per state. Any measured value below 4.5:1 fails.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-17 | The player character, the cacti, and the ground line each have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against the background they are rendered against, in every state and background variation. This is the owner's WCAG AA threshold for non-text game elements.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Capture in-run screenshots covering every background variation the game produces. For each of the three element types, sample representative rendered pixels of the element and of the adjacent background and compute the contrast ratio. Record measured ratios per element per background. Any measured value below 3:1 fails.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-18 | The rendered game is colour-bearing and not the monochrome styling of the reference game: the character, the obstacles and the ground or background are rendered in distinct, visibly saturated hues rather than in greyscale. CONDITIONAL - see the verification note.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Sample rendered pixels from the character, an obstacle and the ground or background. Confirm at least three distinct hues with non-zero saturation. NOTE: the machine check above is the objective half only; whether the result is 'modern and colourful' is the owner's judgement under the final_user_visible_acceptance gate, and ISS-20260809-028 records that this requirement is absent from the approvals.json rationale text.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-19 | On every run end, the game produces one score-trace record containing at minimum three fields: score (integer, final session score), endedAt (ISO-8601 string with an explicit UTC offset) and sessionLengthMs (integer milliseconds).
acceptanceCriteria.verification: End a run and inspect the produced record in the page session. Assert all three fields are present, that score is an integer, that endedAt parses as ISO-8601 with an explicit offset, and that sessionLengthMs is an integer. Repeat for three runs of visibly different lengths; three records must exist.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-20 | The trace record's score field equals the final score displayed on the run-end state for that same run, and sessionLengthMs matches the observed duration of that run within a tolerance of 250 ms.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Start an independent stopwatch on the first frame of a run and stop it at the collision. Compare the stopwatch reading against sessionLengthMs and the on-screen final score against the record's score field. Repeat for one short run under ten seconds and one run over thirty seconds.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-21 | sessionLengthMs is derived from a monotonic time source, not from the difference of two wall-clock readings, so that a change to the system clock during a run does not corrupt the measured session length.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Start a run, change the operating-system clock by one hour mid-run, then end the run. Confirm sessionLengthMs still reflects the real elapsed duration within the AC-20 tolerance. Independently, inspect the implementation reference for the time source used.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-22 | Score-trace records accumulate in page memory for the lifetime of the page session across restarts, are observable in-page, and are discarded when the page unloads. They are written to no persistent store and transmitted to no destination.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Play three runs without reloading and confirm three records are present in the page session. Reload the page and confirm zero records are present. Throughout, confirm localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB and cookies contain no key created by the game, and the network panel shows zero outbound requests.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-23 | Unit 1 persists nothing. After playing any number of runs, reloading the page returns the game to a state indistinguishable from a first visit: no personal best, no score history, no preference, no identifier.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Play at least three runs with varying scores, reload, and compare the idle state screenshot against a screenshot taken from a fresh browser profile that has never loaded the game. The two must be equivalent. Confirm all four storage mechanisms are empty of game-created keys.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-24 | Unit 1 makes no network request after the initial asset load, and remains fully playable with the network disabled.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Load the entry point with the network panel recording. Note the requests made during initial load and confirm all are same-origin static assets. Then set the browser to offline and complete a full journey - start, jump, collide, restart, collide. Confirm the journey completes and that zero further requests were made.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-25 | Unit 1 contains no identity surface: no nickname entry, no account, no sign-in, no profile field and no device or player identifier anywhere in the interface or in the score trace.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Inspect all three states and enumerate every input field, button and label. The expected count of identity-related elements is zero. Inspect a score-trace record and confirm it carries no field naming or identifying a person or device.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-26 | The complete set of states reachable by any keyboard input from the entry point is exactly three: idle, running, run-end. No leaderboard, score table, catalogue, settings, profile, lobby or presence view is reachable.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: From the entry point, exhaustively press every key on the keyboard in each state and record every distinct state entered. The resulting set must contain exactly the three named states and no other. Any additional reachable view fails this criterion.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-27 | Exactly one playable character is present and it is the default. No character selection, catalogue, unlock state, points balance or currency of any kind exists in Unit 1.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Inspect all three states for any character selection affordance, catalogue, locked item, points counter or balance. The expected count is zero. Confirm the character rendered is identical across at least five consecutive runs.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-28 | Every file created or modified by the delivery lies inside the agreed write boundary in D:/os-test/dino-dash-app, and no file under engineering/, .development-os/, DEVELOPMENT.md, development-os.config.json, or anywhere in the product workspace D:/os-test/dino-dash, is created or modified by application code.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Produce the changed-file inventory for the delivery revision. Assert every path is within the agreed allowed set and that the intersection with the prohibited set is empty. Independently confirm the product workspace is byte-identical before and after. Any path outside the boundary fails this criterion regardless of whether the code works.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-29 | The score-trace field contract - field names, types, units and timezone convention - is documented in the delivery in a location a Unit 3 author can find, and matches the behaviour observed in AC-19 to AC-22.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Locate the documentation without reading the run-loop source. Predict the three field names, their types and their units from the documentation alone, then compare against an actual record captured in AC-19. Any discrepancy between documentation and behaviour fails this criterion.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC-30 | Automated evidence exists and is reproducible: a stated command runs the automated tests and produces machine-readable results, and a stated command or procedure produces the accessibility evidence for AC-12, AC-14, AC-16 and AC-17.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run each stated command from a clean checkout of the delivery revision and confirm it completes and emits the machine-readable results referenced by GATE-AUTOMATED-TESTS and GATE-ACCESSIBILITY. Evidence must be recorded under .development-os/evidence/ with kind, sha256 and sourceRevision per engineering-result.schema.json.
